extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications carriers, prospective auction applicants, tower proponents, AM broadcast station licensees, broadcast engineers, and FCC auction/tower compliance counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for (1) participating in FCC competitive bidding for universal service support (application contents, anti-collusion, bidding procedures, post-auction obligations) and (2) notification/analysis/mitigation requirements for tower construction or modification near AM broadcast stations and installations on AM towers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of application process
rubrics_metrics.description: The dates and procedures for submitting applications to participate in competitive bidding pursuant to this subpart shall be announced by public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the public notice for deadlines and procedures; public notice may also specify additional required information or deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application identity and ownership information
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must provide the identity of the applicant (the party that seeks support) and the ownership information as set forth in § 1.2112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full identity and ownership disclosures in an acceptable form; ownership details affect controlling-interest determinations and filing limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized bidders identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must identify the identities of up to three individuals authorized to make or withdraw a bid on behalf of the applicant. No person may serve as an authorized bidder for more than one auction applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List authorized bidders exactly; an individual cannot act as authorized bidder for multiple applicants in the same auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of real parties in interest and related agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must identify all real parties in interest to, and provide a brief description of, any agreements relating to the applicant's participation in the competitive bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose parties and describe agreements that affect participation to ensure transparency and detect improper collusion or control arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of disclosed partnerships/joint ventures/consortia
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that its application contains a brief description of, and identifies each party to, any partnerships, joint ventures, consortia or other agreements, arrangements or understandings of any kind relating to participation in the competitive bidding and the support being sought, including any agreements that address or communicate directly or indirectly bids, bidding strategies, or post-auction market structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification requires explicit disclosure of any coordinating arrangements that could affect bidding or market structure, including indirect communications about prices or strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-collusion certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that it (and any party that controls or is controlled by the applicant) has not entered and will not enter into agreements, arrangements, or understandings with other applicants that address or communicate, directly or indirectly, bidding at auction (including specific prices) or bidding strategies or post-auction market structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong prohibition intended to prevent coordination among bidders; certification is required unless rules/public notice explicitly allow otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls for multiple applications or interests
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant has ownership or other interest with respect to more than one application in a given auction, it must implement internal controls that preclude any individual acting for the applicant from possessing information about the bids or bidding strategies of more than one party submitting an application or communicating such information to anyone possessing such information regarding another party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal controls must effectively segregate sensitive bidding information; implementation does not prevent investigation if prohibited communications are suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole responsibility for evaluating bids and operational capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that it has sole responsibility for investigating and evaluating all technical and marketplace factors affecting its bid level, and that if it wins support it will be able to build and operate facilities in accordance with applicable obligations and Commission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be prepared to justify bidding decisions independently and demonstrate capability to perform if awarded support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance certification with anti-communication rules (§1.21002)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that the applicant and all applicable parties have complied with and will continue to comply with § 1.21002 (prohibition of certain communications during the competitive bidding process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms awareness of and adherence to anti-collusion rules throughout auction participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of statutory and regulatory eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that it is in compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements for receiving the universal service support sought, or (if allowed by mechanism rules) acknowledges that it must be in compliance before authorization to receive support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should verify eligibility requirements specific to the support mechanism and be prepared to document compliance prior to authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default payment/forfeiture acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that it will be subject to a default payment or forfeiture in the event of an auction default and that it will make any payment that may be required pursuant to § 1.21004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand potential financial liabilities for default and ensure funds/bonds are available as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: No delinquent federal debt certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must certify that it is not delinquent on any debt owed to the Commission and not delinquent on any non-tax debt owed to any Federal agency as of the application deadline, or that it will cure any such delinquency prior to the end of the application resubmission period established by public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delinquent debts can render applications unacceptable; applicants should resolve delinquencies or cure them in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of authorization to submit application
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification that the individual submitting the application is authorized to do so on behalf of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the signer has legal authority; failure to sign or improper authorization is an incurable defect per processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on filing multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In any auction, no individual or entity may file more than one application to participate in competitive bidding or have a controlling interest in more than one application; consortium members each are considered to have a controlling interest in the consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications with overlapping controlling interests may be deemed incomplete; at most one such application may be deemed qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of controlling interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlling interest includes individuals or entities with positive or negative de jure or de facto control (e.g., holding 50% or more voting stock or general partnership interest). Ownership through intervening corporations may be determined by successive multiplication of ownership percentages; de facto control assessed case-by-case with examples (appointing majority of board, authority over senior executives, integral role in management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided rules and examples to assess control for application limits and certification obligations; consortium members are deemed controlling interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of consortium and joint venture for auction applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortium: entity formed to apply as a single applicant by two or more separate legal entities. Joint venture: legally cognizable entity formed to apply as a single applicant by two or more separate legal entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formation of these entities affects how controlling interests and filing limits are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial prerequisites (bond or deposit)
rubrics_metrics.description: As prerequisite to participating in competitive bidding, an applicant may be required to post a bond or place funds on deposit with the Commission in an amount based on the default payment or forfeiture that may be required pursuant to § 1.21004; details/deadline announced by public notice. No interest paid on deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be prepared for financial posting requirements and follow public notice instructions on timing and amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and completeness of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any timely submitted application will be reviewed for completeness and compliance; no untimely applications will be reviewed or considered. Applications lacking identity or required certifications are unacceptable and cannot be corrected after the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet filing deadlines and include all required certifications; certain defects (e.g., missing signature) are incurable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple applications by same control scenario
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual or entities commonly controlled submit multiple applications in a single auction, at most one may be deemed complete; others will be deemed incomplete and applicants will not be qualified to bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overlapping ownership submissions; structure applications to comply with single-application limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond/deposit requirement to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant will not be permitted to participate in competitive bidding if it has not provided any bond or deposit required pursuant to the financial requirement paragraph as of the applicable deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required financial deposits are in place by deadline to avoid ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and cure opportunities and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission provides a limited opportunity to cure defects (except failure to sign or make required certifications) during a resubmission period established by public notice; during that period applications may be amended to cure identified defects or make minor amendments. After resubmission period, only minor amendments or corrections allowed; major modifications (e.g., changes in ownership amounting to assignment or transfer of control) are prohibited and will render application newly filed if made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish major vs minor amendments; respond promptly during resubmission period; missing signature and required certifications are not curable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failing to cure defects
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant that fails to cure defects in a timely manner during the resubmission period will have its application dismissed with no further opportunity for resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely cure is essential; dismissal is final for that auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public identification of qualified applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants found qualified to participate in competitive bidding shall be identified in a public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified status is publicly announced; monitor public notices for status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing obligation to amend pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants have a continuing obligation to make any amendments or modifications necessary to maintain accuracy and completeness of information in pending applications, to be made promptly and in no case more than five business days after awareness of the need or after the reportable event occurs. This obligation continues until amendments are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate records and update applications within five business days of any reportable change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'applicant' for communications prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of § 1.21002, 'applicant' includes all controlling interests in the entity submitting an application, holders of partnership and other ownership interests, any stock interest amounting to 10% or more of the entity (outstanding stock or voting stock), and all officers and directors; in a consortium each member is considered to have a controlling interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition means many individuals/entities are covered by anti-communication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'bids' and 'bidding strategies'
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms 'bids' or 'bidding strategies' include capital calls or requests for additional funds in support of bids or bidding strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial coordination such as capital calls can constitute prohibited communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain communications after application deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: After the deadline for submitting applications, an applicant is prohibited from cooperating or collaborating with any other applicant with respect to its own, one another's, or any other competing applicant's bids or bidding strategies, and from communicating the substance of bids or bidding strategies in any manner, until after the post-auction deadline for winning bidders to submit applications for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict anti-collusion rule applies during the bidding period; communications that reveal bid substance or strategy are barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative examples of permitted vs prohibited communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: Ownership overlaps and cross-investments require certification that the overlapping owner will not communicate about bids/strategies with specified other parties, or that it has not and will not communicate with relevant applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples to understand acceptable certifications when ownership interests overlap; certifications must be truthful and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal controls requirement to prevent information sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party with disclosed interests in more than one application must implement internal controls that preclude individuals acting on behalf of the applicant from possessing or communicating bidding information about more than one party in the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal controls are required but do not shield from enforcement if evidence shows prohibited communications occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to modify application for ownership or consortium changes
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must modify its auction application to reflect any changes in ownership or in membership of a consortium or joint venture or agreements/understandings related to the support being sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update applications promptly upon changes in control or membership to remain accurate and compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to report potentially prohibited communications
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant that makes or receives communications that may be prohibited must report such communications to Commission staff immediately, and in any case no later than five business days after the communication occurs. The obligation continues until the report is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reporting is mandated; failure to report could lead to enforcement action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for reporting prohibited communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports required under this section shall be filed as directed in public notices for the specific bidding procedures; if no public notice directs, reports shall be filed in writing to the Chief of the Auctions Division, Office of Economics and Analytics, by the most expeditious means available, including email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow public notice filing instructions; if none, contact Chief of Auctions Division promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of competitive bidding procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed competitive bidding procedures shall be established by public notice prior to the commencement of competitive bidding when the Commission directs bidding pursuant to this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice will describe the specific procedures used for a particular auction; applicants must follow those procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid collection procedure options
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish procedures for collecting bids in single or multiple rounds; item-by-item or aggregated specifications; contingencies linking bids on same/multiple items; bids specifying a support level or indicating demand; multi-stage bids and transitions between stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auction may be designed flexibly; bidders should review public notice for format (e.g., rounds, package bids, staged bidding) and bid submission mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for assigning winning bids beyond price
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may specify procedures for scoring bids by factors in addition to bid amount (e.g., population coverage or geographic contour) and may incorporate public interest considerations into assigning winning bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning determination may consider non-price metrics; bidders should understand scoring factors before bidding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for determining payments and support amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish procedures to determine the amount of support for which winning bidders may be authorized, including support based on amount as bid or other pricing rules, uniform or discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment determination can vary (amount bid vs pricing rules); understand payment rules ahead of bidding to assess financial exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: limits on available information
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may impose limits on the public availability of information about applicants, applications, and bids during the competitive bidding process, and may set procedures for reporting receipt of non-public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information disclosure during auction may be restricted; respect confidentiality rules and reporting obligations for non-public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: sequencing and grouping of eligible areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish one or more groups of eligible areas and the sequence of groups for which bids will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequencing affects bidding strategy; check grouping and order in public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: reserve price policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish reserve prices, disclosed or undisclosed, above which bids would not win in the auction; reserve prices may apply individually, in combination, or in aggregate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve prices can prevent awards above certain levels; bidders should be aware of potential undisclosed reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: timing and method of placing bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may set methods and times for submission of bids, whether remotely, telephonically, electronically, or in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified submission channels and timing precisely to ensure bids are accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: opening bids and bid increments
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may set maximum or minimum opening bids and may announce maximum or minimum bid increments before or during the auction in dollar or percentage terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for increment and opening bid constraints that influence bidding dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: bid withdrawals
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may provide procedures by which bidders may withdraw bids, if withdrawals are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal policies vary; know whether/when withdrawals are permitted and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: stopping procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish procedures regarding when bidding will stop for a round, stage, or entire auction to terminate the auction in a reasonable time consistent with public interest, goals, requirements, and any reserve prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stopping rules affect auction duration and strategy (e.g., activity requirements, end-condition triggers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: activity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may establish activity rules that require a minimum amount of bidding activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activity rules can require continued bidding engagement to retain eligibility; monitor and comply to avoid loss of bidding eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms: auction delay, suspension, or cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice may set procedures for announcing delay, suspension, or cancellation of the auction in the event of natural disaster, technical obstacle, network disruption, security breach, unlawful bidding activity, administrative or weather necessity, or other reasons affecting fair and efficient conduct; procedures for resuming or cancelling the auction are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auctions may be paused or cancelled; follow public notices for instructions on resumption, restarting at a particular round, or cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportioning package bids among geographic areas
rubrics_metrics.description: If package bidding for combinations of geographic areas is adopted, the public notice must establish a methodology for apportioning such bids among geographic areas within the package for purposes of implementing any rule requiring a discrete bid per geographic area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand apportionment methodology to evaluate how package bids map to area-specific awards and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of competitive bidding results
rubrics_metrics.description: After conclusion of competitive bidding, a public notice shall identify winning bidders that may apply for offered support, the amounts of support for which they may apply, and detail application procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-auction public notice signals next steps for winning bidders; follow result notice for application deadlines and required filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winning bidder timely application obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: A winning bidder has a binding obligation to apply for support by the applicable deadline. Failure to file by the deadline or failure to be authorized to receive support constitutes default on the bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely post-auction application is mandatory; missing the deadline triggers default consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to prosecute post-auction application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may dismiss a winning bidder's application with prejudice for failure to prosecute, failure to respond substantially within specified timeframes to official correspondence or requests for information, or failure to comply with requirements for authorization to receive support. Dismissal constitutes default on bid(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to Commission requests and pursue authorization vigorously to avoid dismissal and default liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for default payment or forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: A winning bidder that defaults is liable for either a default payment or a forfeiture, calculated by a method established prior to bidding; if default payment is set as a percentage of the defaulted bid amount, it will not exceed 20% of that amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the default calculation method in the auction-specific public notice and the 20% cap if percentage-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional liabilities for defaulting winning bidders
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to default payment or forfeiture, a defaulting winning bidder may be subject to other measures including disqualification from future competitive bidding under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default has broader consequences beyond monetary liability, potentially barring future participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of AM-tower protection subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: Part protects AM broadcast station operations from nearby tower construction that may distort AM antenna patterns; parties proposing to construct or significantly modify towers near AM antennas or to install antennas on AM towers are responsible for completing required analysis and notice processes and for correcting disturbances if they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tower proponents and parties seeking to locate antennas on structures near AM stations must follow the subprocess (analysis, notice, mitigation) before construction or prior to proposing a location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of AM wavelength
rubrics_metrics.description: AM wavelength (meters) = 300 meters / (AM frequency in megahertz). Example: 1000 kHz (1 MHz) → wavelength = 300 meters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this formula to compute distances defined in terms of wavelength for applicability thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of tower height in electrical degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Tower height in electrical degrees = (Tower height in meters / AM wavelength in meters) × 360 degrees. Example: 75 meters at 1 MHz (300 m wavelength) = 90 electrical degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert physical heights to electrical degrees to determine whether notification/analysis thresholds are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and analysis threshold for nondirectional AM stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents of construction/modification of a tower within one wavelength of a nondirectional AM station and taller than 60 electrical degrees at the AM frequency must notify the AM station at least 30 days in advance and examine potential impact as described; if construction would distort radiation pattern by more than 2 dB, proponent must install and maintain detuning apparatus necessary to restore operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute distance and electrical degrees; if both thresholds met, perform required analysis (moment method), notify 30 days in advance, and plan for detuning if >2 dB distortion predicted or measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and analysis threshold for directional AM stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents of construction/modification of a tower within the lesser of 10 wavelengths or 3 kilometers of a directional AM station and taller than 36 electrical degrees must notify the AM station at least 30 days in advance and examine potential impact; if resulting radiation exceeds licensed standard pattern or augmented standard pattern values, the proponent must install and maintain detuning apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the lesser-of test (10 wavelengths vs 3 km) and 36 electrical-degree height threshold; perform analyses and plan mitigation if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moment method analysis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents within the specified distances must examine potential effects using a moment method analysis consisting of a model of the AM antenna together with the potential re-radiating tower in a lossless environment, employing the methodology specified in § 73.151(c) except AM antenna elements may be modeled as thin wires driven to produce the required radiation pattern without requiring tower impedance measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 73.151(c) methodology with permitted modeling simplifications; use moment method modeling to predict effects and inform mitigation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of significant modification to a tower
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant modification is: (1) any change that would alter the tower's physical height by 5 electrical degrees or more at the AM frequency; or (2) the addition or replacement of one or more antennas or transmission lines on a tower that has been detuned or base-insulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed changes against the 5 electrical degree threshold or installations on detuned/base-insulated towers to determine if procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building-mounted antenna modifications considered subject to rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition/modification of an antenna or antenna-supporting structure on a building is subject to this subpart's analysis/notice requirements only if the height of the antenna-supporting structure alone exceeds the thresholds in the nondirectional/directional paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the antenna-supporting structure height alone for threshold determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement alternative for directional proof stations
rubrics_metrics.description: For an AM station authorized via directional proof based on field strength measurements, the proponent may, instead of the moment method study, demonstrate through measurements taken before and after construction that field strength values at monitoring points do not exceed licensed values; if pre-construction values exceed licensed values, proponent may show post-construction values do not exceed pre-construction values, or AM station may seek authority to increase monitoring-point value after partial proof of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field measurements can substitute modeling for stations licensed by field strength; document pre/post measurements and file required proofs if parameters change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of no significant effect and AM station showing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction outside the specified criteria is presumed to have no significant effect, but an AM station may submit a showing that its operation has been affected consisting of a moment method analysis or field strength measurements. The showing must be provided to the tower proponent/current owner and to the Commission within two years after completion of construction. The Commission may direct installation/maintenance of detuning apparatus if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AM stations have a two-year window to submit a showing; proponents/owners may be directed to mitigate if a showing demonstrates adverse effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on proposing/locating antennas on towers shown to affect AM operation
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for Commission authorization may not propose, and a party holding an authorization may not locate, an antenna on any tower or support structure that has been shown to affect an AM station's operation under this subparagraph, or for which a disputed showing is pending, unless the applicant/party/tower owner notifies the AM station and takes appropriate action to correct the disturbance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not propose or locate antennas on known-affecting towers without completing analysis/notice and remedial measures; notify affected AM station and resolve issues first.

rubrics_metrics.name: AM stations may submit pre-effective-date showings
rubrics_metrics.description: An AM station may submit a showing that its operation was affected by tower construction/modification commenced or completed prior to or on the effective date of these rules; showing must be by moment method analysis or field strength measurements, provided to current tower owner and Commission within one year of effective date; Commission may direct tower owner to install detuning apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legacy constructions can be challenged within one year of rule effective date; tower owners may be required to remediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on proposing/locating antenna on problematic towers (post-2013 rule date)
rubrics_metrics.description: No applicant/party may propose or locate an antenna on any tower/support structure, whether constructed before or after December 5, 2013, that meets the criteria in the notification thresholds, unless the analysis and notice process and necessary corrective measures have been completed by tower owner/proponent/other party prior to construction or prior to proposal/antenna location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these protections to towers both pre- and post-December 5, 2013; ensure analysis and notice are complete before proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installations on nondirectional AM towers: impedance/resistance test and Form 302-AM requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When antennas are installed on a nondirectional AM tower the AM station shall determine operating power by the indirect method. Upon completion, antenna impedance measurements shall be made. If the resistance of the AM antenna changes by more than 2 percent, an application on FCC Form 302-AM (including a tower sketch) shall be filed for the AM station to return to direct power measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform pre/post installation impedance checks; file Form 302-AM within 30 days or with any license application as required if >2% resistance change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installations on directional AM arrays: notice and proof requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before antennas are installed on a tower in a directional AM array, the proponent shall notify the AM station so it may determine operating power by the indirect method and request special temporary authority if necessary. For stations licensed via field strength measurements, a partial proof of performance shall be conducted by the tower proponent both before and after construction. For stations licensed via moment method proof, a base impedance measurement on the modified tower shall be made and retained; if new measured base resistance/reactance differ by more than ±2 ohms and ±4% from modeled values, Form 302-AM must be filed with new impedance measurements and a new moment method model for each pattern where tower is a radiating element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the appropriate measurement/proof path depending on station licensing method; retain records; file Form 302-AM when thresholds exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 302-AM filing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When Form 302-AM is required following an installation, it shall be filed before or simultaneously with any license application associated with the installation. If no license application results, Form 302-AM shall be filed within 30 days after completion of the installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file Form 302-AM as specified to avoid noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum information required in notice of tower construction/modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents subject to notification must provide notice to affected AM stations at least 30 days prior to commencement. Notification must use official licensee info in CDBS (or successor) and include at minimum: proponent's name and address, coordinates of the tower to be constructed/modified, physical description of the planned structure, and results of any analysis showing predicted effect on AM pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete technical details in the 30-day notice; keep written documentation for any oral exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeframe and content to notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to a notification should be made as quickly as possible; any response indicating a potential disturbance must specify technical details and be provided within 30 days. If no response is received within 30 days, the proponent may proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track receipt dates and request expedited response if needed; absence of response after 30 days allows proponent to start construction (subject to later obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for calculating date of receipt for 30-day period
rubrics_metrics.description: If notification is by mail, date of receipt may be ascertained by return receipt on certified mail, enclosure of a dated-return card, or a conservative estimate of mail transit time stated in the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verifiable mailing techniques or state conservative transit estimates to establish clear receipt date for the 30-day clock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited notification option
rubrics_metrics.description: An expedited notification period (less than 30 days) may be requested by the proponent; notification must be identified as 'expedited' and requested response date clearly indicated. Proponent may proceed prior to expiration only upon receipt of written concurrence (or oral with written confirmation to follow) from the affected AM station.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expedited notice only when necessary and obtain concurrence before proceeding early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency temporary tower exception and prompt notice/coop obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: To address immediate/urgent communications needs involving essential public services, a tower proponent may erect a temporary new tower or make a temporary significant modification without prior notice to affected AM stations, provided written notice is given within five days of construction/modification and the proponent cooperates with affected AM stations to promptly remedy any pattern distortions arising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency exceptions permit immediate action but require written notice within five days and cooperation to mitigate any adverse effects.
